# Context-shaped RTL decorations

Original controls generated by `tools/bidi_decoration_fixture.py`. No corpus
content or third-party engine code is used. The reference application exported
`native.pdf`; `tools/record_bidi_decorations.py` records native path bounds and
binds the source, PDF and case inventory by SHA-256.

Sixteen cases cover lam-alef, a lam-alef inside a word, an Arabic joining word,
and Hebrew. Each is split across two runs and repeated with color, underline,
highlight and strikethrough. The first segment alone receives the decoration.
All fonts are requested as Arial; no font files are supplied.

The source uses ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 17.3.2.30 (rtl), 17.3.2.40 (u),
17.3.2.15 (highlight) and 17.3.2.35 (strike). Native glyph advances are a layout
compatibility observation, not a newly claimed normative divergence.

An isolated Arabic prefix can be wider than the finished word. Decorations
must use the final contextual character advances, including the split inside
lam-alef. The native underline of its first character covers half the advance.
Color is different: the complete lam-alef glyph is red in the first case,
although the alef's run declares blue. The correction intentionally leaves
glyph-color behavior unchanged rather than applying caret clipping to it.

Browser validation checks the twelve decoration start/width pairs against
native paths with a 0.2pt tolerance, and preserves every original package part
through the read-only download path. All three native/application page pairs
were inspected. The source stays read-only because complete RTL editing is
not implemented. The subsequent `run-background-height` controls establish the
shared background-height correction, including these exact-spaced lines.
Arbitrary colored shaping clusters remain separate work. This fixture does not
certify full RTL rendering or editing.
